_comment: Generated by scripts/opxy-assets.mjs from src/opxy/manifest.json. Do not edit by hand.

machines.name: Beacon
machines.description: A pulse train through a comb 'lens' that focuses it into a pitch, swept by a rotating light, softened by fog.

machines.name: Bellows
machines.description: A free-reed voice blown by a bellows whose pressure sags and recovers; leaks add breath, a second reed beats against the first.

machines.name: Drill
machines.description: Phase distortion driven by a gear train: the read phase turns with a toothed wheel at a set ratio, stepped by its teeth, rounded by wear, pushed in by bite.

machines.name: Kiln
machines.description: Modal synthesis of fired ceramic: a struck bowl whose glaze damps it and whose cracks make it inharmonic.

machines.name: Lattice
machines.description: A 2D waveguide plate: a metal sheet held at its edges, struck at one point and heard at another. Size sets the mesh, tension its stiffness, damp how fast it rings out, pickup where it's heard.

machines.name: Pylon
machines.description: An aeolian harp: a span of power line sung by the wind. Wind speed sets which of the wire's modes the shed vortices lock onto, span sets how close those modes sit, gust makes the lock wander, and a mains hum sits under it.

machines.name: Silt
machines.description: Additive partials that settle like sediment: each note stirs the high partials up, and they sink back at the settling rate.

machines.name: Spool
machines.description: A single-cycle wave written onto a short tape loop that wears with every pass; bias and wow colour it.

machines.name: Tide
machines.description: Eight tuned resonators in a rock pool, rung by noise that arrives in waves; the note sets the pool's tuning.

machines.name: Vapor
machines.description: A breathy formant voice: a glottal pulse through a throat tube and vowel formants, gliding between vowels.

machines.name: Bell
machines.description: A compressor as a diving bell: depth is the threshold, the air pocket is the release, the knee is how the bell settles.

machines.name: Canyon
machines.description: Multi-tap echo shaped by canyon walls: the distance sets the delay, walls set the tap count, rock absorbs highs, wind modulates.

machines.name: Crease
machines.description: A wavefolder for any track: the signal is folded back on itself like paper, with symmetry and a soft paper limit.

machines.name: Eddy
machines.description: A rotating speaker drowned in turbulence: spin sets the rotor, flutter adds eddies to its speed, depth sets the doppler.

machines.name: Hinge
machines.description: A swinging-door freeze: the door catches a slice of the send's sound and swings it back and forth, creaking as it slows.

machines.name: Lathe
machines.description: A record-cutting lathe on the send: the signal is cut into a lacquer groove, saturating at the cutter, then played back with inner-groove loss, wear and rumble.

machines.name: Nave
machines.description: A send reverb modelled on a stone nave: the nave's length sets the decay, the stone's hardness how long the highs survive, the choir's carving how densely the echoes diffuse, and the west doors how long before the first reflection arrives.

machines.name: Relay
machines.description: A bucket-brigade delay with failing stages: a chain of charge buckets passes the signal along on each clock tick; some buckets leak, the clock wanders, and the output recirculates to the input.

machines.name: Sieve
machines.description: A harmonic sieve: a comb filter tuned to the input's fundamental keeps only chosen multiples, shaken to let others through.

machines.name: Tilt
machines.description: Tilt-shift for sound: a spectral tilt about a focal band, with a blur that smears everything outside the band in frequency and in time.

machines.name: Ants
machines.description: A note player on aux track 12: ants walk a lattice of scale degrees leaving scent; trails strengthen into repeated phrases and fade when unused.

machines.name: Ebb
machines.description: A track-control player on aux track 12: notes rise and fall with a tide over a scale; the tide's height picks the register, foam scatters grace notes at the turn.

machines.name: Ferry
machines.description: A track-control player on aux track 12: a ferry runs a route between ports (the held chord's tones), dwells at each port before it plays it, and swell holds it up on the way.

machines.name: Flock
machines.description: A note player on aux track 12: a small flock flies over a two-octave pitch field and each bird plays the scale degree under it as it crosses into a new cell. Cohesion pulls the notes into a cluster, speed sets how often they come, scatter lets birds break off.

machines.name: Gears
machines.description: A track-control player on aux track 12: two meshed spur gears, each tooth that meshes plays a note on the target track; the wheels' tooth ratio sets a polyrhythm between their revolutions.

machines.name: Lichen
machines.description: A lichen player on aux track 12: a colony grows across a lattice of scale degrees and registers, spreading into neighbouring cells and dying back from its old centre; every cell it newly grows into plays on another track. Its own track stays silent.

machines.name: Marble
machines.description: A Galton board player on aux track 12: marbles drop through rows of pegs into bins pitched on a scale, and the pile they make is the distribution of notes sent to the target track.

machines.name: Pendula
machines.description: A pendulum wave on aux track 12: pendulums of slowly different lengths each play a note on the target track as they cross the centre, drifting in and out of phase. Length sets the longest pendulum's swing, count how many hang, swing how wide (and so how hard) they swing, scale which notes they play.

machines.name: Rain
machines.description: A rain player on aux track 12: drops fall on a roof of pitched tiles at a rate, gusts push them across the tiles, puddles repeat the last notes. It plays another track; its own track stays silent.

machines.name: Ringer
machines.description: Change ringing on aux track 12: a ring of bells permuted by a method, one change per row, at a steady pace, each blow played as a note on the target track. Bells sets the stage (4 to 12), method the permutation rule, pace the blows per beat, stroke the handstroke gap.
